decision: Use a coordinator-side stable byte+metadata digest snapshotter for MissionStore and DurableRequestJournal during read-only Qubes Phase-1 qualification.
winner: stable regular-file digest with inode/mtime/ctime/size/content binding and fail-closed retries

criteria.correctness: Detects content changes, atomic replacement, and same-content rewrites that a content-only hash can miss; absent files have a deterministic sentinel state.
criteria.robustnessSecurity: Rejects symlinks/non-regular files and fails closed if a target changes while sampled. Imports no MissionQueue or journal mutation APIs and returns digests only, not state contents or paths.
criteria.latency: Two small local file reads per snapshot plus SHA-256; no qrexec/network round trip is added by the adapter itself.
criteria.resourceUse: No daemon, database, WAL, persistent watcher, or production state. Memory is bounded by the two state files being hashed.
criteria.regressionRisk: New isolated adapter and tests; no changes to MissionQueue, WorkerRuntime, coordinator mutation semantics, or transport protocol.
criteria.qa: Syntax and focused node:test coverage are wired into DIG Qubes Transport QA before the existing transport suite. Local focused validation passed before commit review.

alternatives.name: content-only SHA-256
alternatives.lesson: Same-content rewrite or atomic replacement can mutate durable state while preserving bytes, so bytes alone are insufficient evidence.

alternatives.name: semantic JSON digest
alternatives.lesson: Normalizing JSON can hide writes such as savedAt changes and weakens zero-mutation evidence.

alternatives.name: persistent filesystem watcher
alternatives.lesson: Can improve transient-write observability but adds lifecycle/platform complexity and still needs OS-specific guarantees; not required to unblock the current snapshotMutationState interface.

alternatives.name: state-changing smoke test first
alternatives.lesson: Expands blast radius before policy/routing zero-mutation qualification is proven.

knownLimitations: Before/after snapshots cannot by themselves prove that no transient write-and-rollback occurred entirely between samples. Real-Qubes readiness should additionally rely on the dedicated read-only service boundary and coordinator-side OS permissions/policy that deny writes.
Executable GitHub-hosted QA remains a separate readiness gate.
